test_cases.objective: To verify that the system accurately tracks inventory quantities in real-time through standard database updates.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
User has appropriate access to the inventory management module.
At least one item is set up in the item master.

test_steps.action: Perform a manual inventory adjustment (e.g., add 10 units of a specific item).
test_steps.expected_result: The system reflects the updated inventory quantity for the item within 30 seconds.

test_steps.action: Perform a picking transaction to remove 5 units of the same item.
test_steps.expected_result: The system reflects the reduced inventory quantity for the item within 30 seconds.

acceptance_criteria: All inventory quantity updates are reflected in the system within the specified 30-second timeframe.
The system accurately displays the current inventory levels after each transaction.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-006: Track inventory quantities in real-time using standard database updates.
data_integrity_requirements: Inventory quantities must be accurate and reflect all transactions.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Standard Report Generation for Inventory Movements
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system can generate standard inventory movement reports using pre-built templates within the specified time.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
User has appropriate access to reporting functions.
Sufficient inventory transaction data exists to generate a meaningful report.

test_steps.action: Navigate to the reporting module and select the 'Inventory Movement Report' using a pre-built template.
test_steps.expected_result: The system presents options to filter or define the scope of the report (e.g., date range, item type).

test_steps.action: Define a specific date range for the report (e.g., last 7 days) and initiate report generation.
test_steps.expected_result: The inventory movement report is generated and displayed within 5 minutes.

test_steps.action: Verify that the generated report accurately reflects the inventory movements within the specified date range.
test_steps.expected_result: The report details include item movements (receipts, issues, adjustments) with correct quantities and dates.
data_to_capture: Comparison of report data with known transaction logs

acceptance_criteria: Standard inventory movement reports can be generated using pre-built templates.
Reports are generated within the specified 5-minute timeframe.
The generated reports accurately reflect the inventory movements based on the defined criteria.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-009: Create inventory movement reports using pre-built templates.
data_integrity_requirements: Inventory movement reports must be accurate and complete.

test_cases.objective: To verify that the system correctly implements First-In-First-Out (FIFO) inventory rotation for stock management.
prerequisites: System is configured with multiple batches of the same item having different received dates.
User has appropriate permissions to manage inventory.

test_steps.action: Add multiple batches of the same raw material to inventory, ensuring each batch has a distinct received date.
test_steps.expected_result: Each batch is recorded in the system with its respective received date.

test_steps.action: Initiate a stock withdrawal or consumption for a quantity of the raw material.
test_steps.expected_result: The system deducts inventory from the oldest received batch first, adhering to FIFO principles.

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully deducts inventory from the oldest batch when a withdrawal is initiated.
The system accurately reflects the remaining quantities for all affected batches.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-003: Implement First-In-First-Out (FIFO) inventory rotation using vendor default algorithms.
data_integrity_requirements: Inventory quantities must be accurately updated after stock withdrawal.
Batch dates must be correctly maintained and used for rotation logic.

test_cases.objective: To verify that the system correctly implements First-Expired-First-Out (FEFO) inventory rotation for expiry date management.
prerequisites: System is configured with multiple batches of the same item having different expiry dates.
User has appropriate permissions to manage inventory.

test_steps.action: Add multiple batches of the same packaging component to inventory, ensuring each batch has a distinct expiry date.
test_steps.expected_result: Each batch is recorded in the system with its respective expiry date.

test_steps.action: Initiate a stock withdrawal or consumption for a quantity of the packaging component.
test_steps.expected_result: The system deducts inventory from the batch with the earliest expiry date first, adhering to FEFO principles.

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully deducts inventory from the earliest expiring batch when a withdrawal is initiated.
The system accurately reflects the remaining quantities for all affected batches.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-004: Support First-Expired-First-Out (FEFO) rotation for expiry date management.
data_integrity_requirements: Inventory quantities must be accurately updated after stock withdrawal.
Expiry dates must be correctly maintained and used for rotation logic.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Barcode Scanning Integration for Inventory Updates
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system correctly updates inventory quantities when using barcode scanning functionality.
prerequisites: Barcode scanner is connected and configured.
Inventory items have valid barcodes assigned in the system.
System is in a state where inventory can be added/updated.

test_steps.action: Scan the barcode of a specific inventory item using the integrated barcode scanner.
test_steps.expected_result: The system recognizes the scanned barcode and displays the corresponding item details.
data_to_capture: Item details displayed by the system

test_steps.action: Enter a quantity to be added or removed for the scanned item and confirm the transaction.
test_steps.expected_result: The inventory quantity for the item is updated in real-time according to the entered quantity.

test_steps.action: Verify the updated inventory quantity for the item through the system's inventory view.
test_steps.expected_result: The displayed inventory quantity accurately reflects the addition or removal performed in the previous step.

acceptance_criteria: Inventory quantities are updated accurately after barcode scanning and transaction confirmation.
The system correctly identifies items based on their barcodes.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-007: Support barcode scanning using vendor's barcode integration module.
data_integrity_requirements: Inventory quantities must be accurate and reflect all scanned transactions.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Cycle Count Schedule Generation and Execution
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system can generate cycle count schedules based on predefined criteria and that these schedules can be executed.
prerequisites: Sufficient inventory data exists in the system.
Cycle count scheduling parameters (e.g., frequency, item selection criteria) are configured.
User has permissions to generate and execute cycle counts.

test_steps.action: Initiate the generation of a cycle count schedule based on configured parameters.
test_steps.expected_result: The system generates a cycle count schedule listing specific items and locations to be counted.
data_to_capture: List of items and locations in the schedule

test_steps.action: Select a specific item from the generated schedule and perform a physical count of that item.
test_steps.expected_result: The system allows for the input of the physically counted quantity for the selected item.

test_steps.action: Enter the physically counted quantity into the system against the scheduled item.
test_steps.expected_result: The system records the entered physical count.

test_steps.action: Execute the cycle count for the item, allowing the system to reconcile the physical count with the system's recorded quantity.
test_steps.expected_result: The system indicates whether the physical count matches the system's recorded quantity or flags a discrepancy.

acceptance_criteria: Cycle count schedules are generated accurately according to configured parameters.
The system correctly records physical counts and flags discrepancies.
The cycle count process can be successfully executed for scheduled items.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-008: Create inventory movement reports using pre-built templates.
URS-INV-018: Generate inventory accuracy reports using standard reconciliation features.
data_integrity_requirements: Physical counts must be accurately recorded and reconciled with system data.
Discrepancies must be clearly identified for investigation.

test_cases.test_name: Verify User Access Controls and Role-Based Security
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system enforces user access controls and role-based security as defined by vendor specifications.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
User accounts with different roles (e.g., Administrator, Warehouse Operator, Viewer) are created.
Documentation for vendor's role-based security is available.

test_steps.action: Log in to the system using an Administrator account.
test_steps.expected_result: Administrator can access all system functionalities and settings.

test_steps.action: Log out and log in using a Warehouse Operator account.
test_steps.expected_result: Warehouse Operator can perform inventory management tasks (e.g., receiving, picking, adjustments) but cannot access administrative settings or user management.

test_steps.action: Log out and log in using a Viewer account.
test_steps.expected_result: Viewer can only view inventory data and reports, with no ability to modify any data or access system settings.

test_steps.action: Attempt to perform an action restricted to a higher role (e.g., Viewer attempting to adjust inventory).
test_steps.expected_result: The system prevents the action and displays an appropriate error message indicating insufficient permissions.

acceptance_criteria: Users can only access functionalities permitted by their assigned roles.
Unauthorized access attempts are blocked and logged.
The system correctly enforces role-based security as per vendor documentation.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-017: Support user access controls through vendor's role-based security.
data_integrity_requirements: System configuration for roles and permissions remains unchanged unless authorized.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Inventory Audit Trail and Transaction History Archiving
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system maintains a comprehensive audit trail for all inventory transactions and supports the archiving of transaction history.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
Sufficient inventory transactions have been performed to test archiving.
Documentation for vendor's logging and archiving functionality is available.

test_steps.action: Perform a series of inventory transactions (e.g., receiving, issuing, adjustments, transfers) for various items.
test_steps.expected_result: Each transaction is recorded in the system's audit trail with details such as user, timestamp, item, quantity, and transaction type.
data_to_capture: Audit trail entries for each transaction

test_steps.action: Access and review the audit trail for the performed transactions.
test_steps.expected_result: The audit trail accurately reflects all performed transactions and their associated details.
data_to_capture: Comparison of performed transactions vs. audit trail entries

test_steps.action: Initiate the archiving process for historical transaction data according to vendor specifications.
test_steps.expected_result: The system successfully archives the specified historical transaction data.

test_steps.action: Attempt to access or modify archived transaction data through the primary inventory interface.
test_steps.expected_result: Archived data is not accessible or modifiable through the standard user interface, confirming it has been moved to an archive.
data_to_capture: Error message or lack of access to archived data

test_steps.action: Verify that the system's data retention policies are correctly applied during the archiving process.
test_steps.expected_result: Only data within the defined retention period is archived, or the archiving process adheres to the configured retention policy.

acceptance_criteria: All inventory transactions are logged in the audit trail.
The audit trail contains accurate and complete information for each transaction.
The system successfully archives historical transaction data.
Archived data is not accessible or modifiable via the standard user interface.
Data retention policies are correctly enforced.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-016: Maintain inventory audit trail using vendor's standard logging functionality.
URS-INV-019: Archive transaction history using vendor's data retention policies.
data_integrity_requirements: Audit trail is immutable and tamper-evident.
Archived data is stored securely and can be retrieved if necessary.
Data integrity is maintained during the archiving process.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Support for Multiple Storage Locations and Location Master Setup
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system correctly supports and manages inventory across multiple defined storage locations using the standard location master setup.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
User has administrative privileges to configure locations.
Access to the system's location master configuration module.

test_steps.action: Navigate to the location master configuration module.
test_steps.expected_result: The location master configuration screen is displayed.

test_steps.action: Create at least three distinct storage locations (e.g., 'WH-A-R1', 'WH-B-R2', 'QC-Area').
test_steps.expected_result: New storage locations are successfully created and listed in the master.

test_steps.action: Assign a specific raw material to each of the newly created storage locations with initial quantities.
test_steps.expected_result: Inventory is successfully recorded against each specified storage location.

test_steps.action: Generate an inventory report filtered by storage location.
test_steps.expected_result: The report accurately displays the inventory quantities for each specified storage location.

acceptance_criteria: The system allows the creation and management of multiple distinct storage locations.
Inventory can be accurately assigned and tracked within each defined storage location.
Inventory reports correctly reflect quantities per storage location.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-010: Support multiple storage locations with standard location master setup.
data_integrity_requirements: Inventory quantities must be accurately associated with the correct storage location.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Reorder Alerts Based on Minimum Stock Levels
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system generates timely and accurate reorder alerts when inventory quantities fall below predefined minimum stock levels.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
User has privileges to configure item master and minimum stock levels.
At least one item is configured with a minimum stock level.
Access to the system's item master and alerting configuration.

test_steps.action: Navigate to the item master configuration module.
test_steps.expected_result: The item master configuration screen is displayed.

test_steps.action: Select an item and configure a minimum stock level (e.g., 50 units).
test_steps.expected_result: The minimum stock level is successfully saved for the selected item.

test_steps.action: Perform inventory transactions (e.g., issue/consume) to reduce the current stock of this item to below the configured minimum level (e.g., 49 units).
test_steps.expected_result: Inventory is updated, and the current stock level is now below the minimum threshold.

test_steps.action: Check the system's alerts or notifications for reorder alerts.
test_steps.expected_result: A reorder alert is generated for the item whose stock has fallen below the minimum level.

test_steps.action: Verify that the alert details correctly identify the item and indicate the need for reordering.
test_steps.expected_result: The alert provides accurate information about the item and the reorder requirement.

acceptance_criteria: The system allows configuration of minimum stock levels for individual items.
Reorder alerts are triggered automatically when stock falls below the configured minimum.
Alerts accurately identify the item requiring reordering and the reason (low stock).
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-011: Generate reorder alerts based on minimum stock levels using standard alerting.
data_integrity_requirements: The system must accurately compare current stock levels against configured minimums to trigger alerts.
